notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: the latest EGX close is Monday 2 November (EGX30 48,403.14), Banque du Caire's first session. Brent is Monday's settlement and Tuesday's early Asian trade. The pound is the CBE's Monday closing rate. US voters go to the polls today. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out or flagged: Monday's foreign flows including deals (Amwal Al Ghad puts foreign net selling at EGP 2.43 bn, against EGP 138.1 mn excluding deals in Masrawy and EnterpriseAM; the edition uses the figure two sources agree on); Monday's breadth and turnover come from one source (Foudalens); October's PMI comes from one report (Rio Times), not the S&P Global release; the Qeshm strike relies on US officials quoted by the Wall Street Journal and Iranian state media; Monday's debt flows; the budget's oil-price assumption; Egypt's October inflation figure.

items: EGX30 falls 1.72% to 48,744.01 in the first session after the hike, with 148 stocks down and only 63 up as Palm Hills drops 7% → higher rates hit developers and consumer lenders while foreign and Arab investors sell; turnover of EGP 7.2 bn is 35% below its 90-day average.

Banque du Caire starts trading today as BQDC at an offer price of EGP 5.30, after a record EGP 205.8 bn of private-placement orders → the debut tests demand in a falling market; retail holders can sell back at EGP 5.30 for 30 days through CI Capital.

The state borrows about EGP 4.3 tn at home in July to October, almost all to refinance, and a finance official says the hike adds EGP 150 bn to the bill → short-dated debt reprices fast, so the 100 bp move feeds straight into the budget; the first post-hike 364-day bill sells at 26.076%.

Brent falls about 3.2% to $109.75 early Monday after Iran says a Qatari-brokered plan could reopen Hormuz within two days → a lower oil price eases Egypt's import bill, but Trump still talks of hitting one or two more targets after Tuesday's midterms.

AMOC reports quarterly sales up 41% to EGP 43.2 bn and net profit up 154% to EGP 3.475 bn → high oil prices and refining margins lift results; the stock rises 2.21% on Sunday against a falling market.

Brent's expiring December contract settles 2.4% higher at $117.64 on Friday, a six-month high, after the first limpet-mine strike on a tanker in Hormuz since February → traders brace for a US strike on Iran after Tuesday's midterms, and Brent ends October up 13.6%, widening Egypt's fuel bill.

Iran says Hormuz stays shut and there are no nuclear talks until the US meets its demands, as one report says US strikes could come as early as 4 November → the risk of a wider war after the midterms keeps oil, shipping and regional risk premiums high as the EGX reopens.

Saudi Arabia agrees to keep a $5.3 bn deposit at the CBE for another year instead of taking it back at end-October, banking sources say → the renewal removes a large maturity just as foreign money leaves Egyptian debt; no official statement confirms it yet.

The first T-bill auction after the hike sets the 364-day yield at 26.076%, up from 25.912% on 27 October, and the state takes EGP 78.84 bn of a EGP 110 bn target → the CBE's 100 bp move is passing into bill yields, which supports bank income but raises the state's borrowing cost.

The pound holds at EGP 56.12 per dollar at the CBE as banks open Sunday at 56.04–56.19 to sell, the first quotes after the hike → the hike has not yet moved the pound, so today's EGX session tests how equities price higher rates.

Brent's expiring December contract settles 2.4% higher at $117.64 on Friday, a six-month high, after the first limpet-mine strike on a tanker in Hormuz since February → traders brace for a US strike on Iran after Tuesday's midterms, and Brent ends October up 13.6%, widening Egypt's fuel bill.

Saudi Arabia agrees to keep a $5.3 bn deposit at the CBE for another year instead of taking it back at end-October, banking sources say → the renewal removes a large maturity just as foreign money leaves Egyptian debt; no official statement confirms it yet.

The first T-bill auction after the hike sets the 364-day yield at 26.076%, up from 25.912% on 27 October, and the state takes EGP 78.84 bn of a EGP 110 bn target → the CBE's 100 bp move is passing into bill yields, which supports bank income and the carry trade but raises the state's borrowing cost.

The S&P 500 falls 1.8% and the Nasdaq 2.9% on Friday after Intel's outlook, while gold drops 3.52% to $3,879.90 → a risk-off week end and forced selling of metals weigh on sentiment toward emerging markets before the EGX reopens.

Qatari mediators in Tehran deliver a Vance letter proposing a new diplomatic process, with a meeting possible within a week in Doha or Istanbul → talks offer a path away from escalation, but reports say Trump has told Gulf allies to prepare for a short, intense campaign after the midterms.

The CBE raises rates by 100 bp to a 20% deposit rate after Thursday's close, its first hike since March 2024, against a Reuters poll that expected a hold → the pound near record lows at EGP 56.12 and heavy foreign selling of local debt push the CBE to defend the carry trade; Sunday is the EGX's first session to price it.

EGX30 rises 0.64% to 49,596.14 on Thursday as Banque du Caire's EGP 36.37 bn offering executes and lifts turnover to EGP 43.9 bn → foreign institutions net buy EGP 29.2 bn, mostly through the bank's offering, while 180 stocks rise and 31 fall before trading in BQDC starts on 2 November.

The IMF targets a staff-level deal on Egypt's final review before mid-December, worth about $2.3 bn in final disbursements → Kozack says talks focus on tight monetary policy, which the CBE's hike now delivers.

Brent rises 1.04% to $116.08 in early Friday trade after settling at $114.88 on Thursday, as a tanker is hit in Hormuz and US strike talk returns → oil near $116 widens Egypt's fuel import bill while pump prices stay frozen.

The ECB and the Bank of Japan both hold, the BoJ at 1.25% by 8-1, while Reuters sources call a 17 December ECB hike all but certain → global policy stays tight after US growth beats forecasts at 3.4%, limiting appetite for emerging-market debt.

The CBE raises rates by 100 bp to a 20% deposit rate, its first hike since March 2024, when most analysts expected a hold → the pound's slide past 56 and about $1.67 bn of foreign and Arab debt selling in three days (derived) push the CBE to defend the carry trade.

The Fed holds at 3.75–4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack voting for a hike, and markets largely price a December hike → elevated inflation and war-driven uncertainty keep US yields high (10-year 5.04%), narrowing the carry that holds foreign money in Egyptian bills.

EGX30 closes Thursday 0.64% higher at 49,596.14 while the EGX70 jumps 2.77% → local buyers absorb foreign selling (foreign institutions net sell EGP 229.1 mn on Wednesday), leaving the index about 2.85% lower over five sessions (derived).
Foreign and Arab net selling of Egyptian bills and bonds slows to $391 mn on Wednesday from $619.1 mn → debt outflows continue but ease as the pound holds at EGP 56.20 at the CBE.

Banque du Caire's retail book closes 27 times covered and the sale is upsized to 45%, with trading expected on 2 November → EGP 49.2 bn of retail orders chase EGP 1.8 bn of stock, showing local appetite for quality state assets even in a falling market.

top.what: The pound strengthens to EGP 55.51 per dollar at the CBE on Monday from 56.12 after the hike, and major banks quote 55.49
top.why: the 100 bp hike and falling oil ease demand for dollars; a firmer pound helps importers and foreign holders of local debt.

top.why: output and new orders fall at the fastest pace in four months and input costs rise at a five-month high.

stories.h: Brent plunges 7.6% as Iran approves talks, then edges up after a US strike on Qeshm
stories.what: Brent for January falls 7.6% to $104.77 on Monday and WTI 7.4% to $96.46, the biggest slump in three months. In early Asian trade on Tuesday Brent rises 0.5% to $105.25 and WTI to $96.93 after reports that a US jet destroys a missile launcher on Iran's Qeshm Island.
stories.why: Iran's supreme leader approves negotiations, according to IRNA, and Trump says he wants to let talks play out; trend-following funds also cut long positions.
stories.aff: Egypt's fuel import bill, the pound, inflation expectations and Gulf budgets.
stories.eg: Each fall in crude lowers the dollar cost of Egypt's fuel imports.
stories.egx: Bullish for importers and energy users; bearish for oil-linked AMOC, which falls 4.61% on Monday.

key.l: Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz once terms are met

stories.h: Iran speeds up its peace plan as the US strikes Qeshm and Americans vote
stories.what: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei gives the government wider authority to speed up talks, and Iran says its seven-step plan to reopen Hormuz and resume nuclear talks could take two days instead of a week. Its terms include lifting the US naval blockade, sanctions relief and a regional ceasefire. On Monday night a US fighter jet destroys a missile launcher on Qeshm Island after an Iranian missile downs a US drone, officials say.
stories.why: Trump says a deal is coming together and that oil has fallen almost $10 a barrel; Vance says any deal needs verifiable nuclear guarantees. US officials describe the Qeshm strike as self-defence, not a return to full combat.
stories.aff: Oil, Gulf shipping, regional risk premiums and Suez traffic.
stories.eg: A reopened Hormuz would ease Egypt's energy costs and help the pound; renewed fighting after today's midterms would reverse that.
stories.egx: Neutral today: the outcome of talks and the midterms will drive oil, the pound and sentiment.

key.l: CBE sell rate, EGP per USD, Mon 2 Nov

stories.h: Pound firms to 55.51 per dollar as oil falls after the CBE's hike
stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; Al Mal; El Balad
stories.what: The CBE's closing rate is 55.37 buy and 55.51 sell on Monday, against 55.99 and 56.12 after the hike on Thursday. National Bank of Egypt and Banque Misr quote 55.39 and 55.49, and Al Mal describes an almost across-the-board fall in the dollar. The first T-bill auction after the hike sold 364-day bills at 26.076%.
stories.why: Higher rates and the fall in oil prices ease pressure on the pound, though none of the sources gives a single cause.
stories.aff: Import costs, inflation expectations, foreign holders of local debt and companies with dollar debt.
stories.eg: A firmer pound lowers the cost of imported fuel and food.
stories.egx: Bullish for importers and foreign-held blue chips; slightly bearish for exporters' pound revenue.

stories.h: EGX30 slips 0.7% as small caps drop more than 2% on the Banque du Caire debut
stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; Cairo Mubasher; Masrawy; EnterpriseAM; Foudalens
stories.what: The EGX30 closes Monday at 48,403.14, down 0.70%, after an intraday low near 47,790. The EGX70 falls 2.23% and the EGX100 2.22%, and market cap loses about EGP 65 bn to EGP 3.832 tn. CIB (+2.88%) and Telecom Egypt (+3.08%) rise, while QNB Egypt (-6.13%), Mopco (-6.14%) and Eastern Company (-5.75%) fall. Foreigners net sell EGP 138.1 mn excluding deals, while Arabs and Egyptians are net buyers.
stories.why: Banque du Caire takes 21.2% of turnover, and an Okaz Asset Management analyst says liquidity and positioning, not valuation, drive prices.
stories.aff: Small and mid caps, fertiliser and tobacco names, and retail investors.
stories.eg: EnterpriseAM puts the EGX30 up 15.7% year to date.
stories.egx: Bearish for small caps and the broad market; CIB holds the index up.
stories.names: CIB, Telecom Egypt (up); QNB Egypt, Mopco, Eastern Company (down).

stories.h: Banque du Caire closes flat on debut as the Treasury takes up to half the proceeds
stories.what: BQDC closes its first session at EGP 5.31, up 0.19%, after hitting EGP 5.68 early and dipping to EGP 5.25. About 373.1 mn shares worth EGP 2.02 bn trade, making it the EGX's most-traded stock, and the bank's market value is EGP 80.98 bn. The Treasury takes up to half the EGP 36.37 bn proceeds, about EGP 18.2 bn, to ease debt.
stories.why: The offer priced at adviser Baker Tilly's fair value, leaving little room for a first-day jump.
stories.aff: Brokers, sentiment toward state listings and the Treasury's financing.
stories.eg: The Cabinet approves giving the Finance Ministry half of the proceeds from state offerings.
stories.egx: Neutral: a stable debut, but no rally to lift sentiment.

stories.h: Non-oil PMI stays at 47.2 as output and orders fall at the fastest pace in four months
stories.what: Egypt's non-oil PMI is 47.2 in October, the same as September and below the 48 forecast, its tenth straight month below 50. Output and new orders fall at the fastest pace in four months, input-cost inflation reaches a five-month high, and employment slips back into contraction.
stories.why: Weak client demand, lower purchasing power and the regional war weigh on activity, while imported materials, energy, shipping and a weaker pound raise costs.
stories.aff: Consumer demand, company margins and jobs.
stories.eg: Weak demand adds to the case that the CBE's hike will hurt growth.
stories.egx: Bearish for consumer and industrial names.

key.l: Petrojet pipeline for Cypriot gas to Damietta

stories.h: Petrojet to build a $170 mn pipeline taking Cypriot gas to Damietta for export
stories.what: State-owned Petrojet wins a $170 mn contract for a 40 km pipeline from the Zohr facilities in Port Said to the Damietta LNG terminal, starting early next year and taking about 12 months. It serves Eni and TotalEnergies' Cronos field off Cyprus, due to start in 1H 2028 and plateau at 500 mmcf/d. Fees could reach about $165 mn a year, and Cairo wants about 25% of the gas for home use. Separately, Iraq, Egypt and Jordan discuss new Red Sea and Mediterranean outlets for Iraqi crude.
stories.why: Eni wants to restart the Damietta LNG plant and restore regular LNG exports from Egypt.
stories.aff: Egypt's gas balance, LNG export income and energy contractors.
stories.eg: Tolling fees and a share of the gas support Egypt's energy and dollar position from 2028.
stories.egx: Mildly bullish for energy services; no listed company is a direct party.

week.why: Trump has said strikes on Iran could follow the vote; oil and the pound react to the result.
The first inflation print after the CBE's 100 bp hike; September urban inflation was 13.9%. CAPMAS usually publishes around the 9th or 10th.
